critic: LEAD (independent critic, checked by a second agent)
verdict:
bags is now a clean final image, and it is the strongest frame on the stage. The handwriting-like streaks at the front of the pool, which were plain to see in the 4c5ff43 frame, are gone. The two silhouettes register with inspection_room match. The type field above the bags is quiet: median 25 graded, p90 28.

The stage still fails, for two reasons:
- **Four of the five published frames are stale.** dawn, dawn_high, cell_close and cell_far are byte-identical to the 4c5ff43 renders (committed 07:18), so every round-3 failure is still in them:
  - Dawn's hands read as dark gloves, the cuffs flare into pale bell sleeves, and the trousers read as stiff tubes.
  - From the front the hair reads as a flat cap, so the figure reads as a man.
  - The shirt bump reads as corrugated stripes.
  - In cell_close the back edge of the pool is a hard arc, the shaft dies above its patch, and the barred patch reads as flat white cards laid on the floor.

  Seven void_stage commits have landed since then: bb6720e, efa6286, e64224b, 4604f1a, 9559a54, 742a943 and 8ea6b03. They include a brighter dawn spot (4600 to 6400 W), a softer edge on the cell spot (blend 0.25 to 0.50), a fill on the lower bunk, the cuff, hand and shaft work, and a seated Dawn in cell_far. None of this can be judged until the frames are re-rendered. The cut also uses six cameras that this code adds (pool, chair, cell_dawn, dawn_close, cell_floor and divide), and none of them has a published frame.
- **The bags plate is only 1280x720.** The lead's 1920 composite is therefore a 1.5x upscale, and a 4 % push makes it 1.56x. COVERAGE already asks for this plate to be rendered larger for the move on 'WHEN? held'.

Two notes on the cut from match:
- **Dawn's case loses most of its brightness.** Its front-pocket median drops from 75 graded to 28. The front still reads: the pocket outline, the zips and the folds are legible. But the left side panel (13-20) is as dark as the black beside it (16-18), and the lower right of the front (22-28) matches the haze to its right (27-31). In those places only the rim and the pool hold the case's outline.
- **The tag vanishes.** The blank luggage tag on the case top in match is gone after the cut. It sits below the Y of YES.

The YES ends 35 px (at 1080) above the case handle. A centred 4 % push closes that gap to about 26 px, so the type crowds the bags. In the cold open, the second YES cuts the registered match plate 9 % tighter, centred on (0.5, 0.56) (PLATE.yes in gfx/type.html). There the handle top lands at about y 231, and its right post runs into the foot of the Y.

bags alone is close to the bar, but the stage as published is not. The scores are unchanged.
answers:
Measured on frames/graded/void_stage/bags.jpg and frames/raw/void_stage/bags.png (1280x720), on the 4c5ff43 bags.jpg and bags.png for comparison, and on out/gfx/cut/bags_yes.png, match_yes.png and match_to_void.mp4 (1920x1080, 24 fps, 96 frames).

1. **Do the two bag silhouettes register with the new inspection_room match? Yes.**

   I overlaid the gradient edges of the two graded frames at 1280. The best match is at zero offset. The outlines coincide all the way round the case body, the trolley handle, the wheels, the duffel's ends, its straps and the base line. Edges differ in only three places: inside the faces (the light changes), at the table edge against the floor, and at the case top (the tag).

   Two things change across the cut:
   - **Value.**
     - The case's front pocket p50 is 75 graded in match and 28 in void (p90 100 against 51).
     - The case's left side panel is about 35 against 16, and the handle 45 against 23.
     - The background beside the bags is about 39-49 in match and 16-29 in void.
     - The duffel hardly moves (14 against 15).
     - Mean frame luminance falls from about 30 to about 20.

     So on the cut the room vanishes, and the case drops from the brightest object in the frame to a dark grey well under the pool. Its upper front still reads (40-80), and the pocket outline, zips and folds stay legible, so it keeps its face. But its left side panel (13-20) is as dark as the black beside it (16-18), and the lower right of its front (22-28) matches the haze to its right (27-31). In those places the outline holds only through the rim and the pool below. The code keeps the faces dark on purpose (see the comment on rim_bags), so how far the case should drop on the cut is a judgement. The optional kicker fix lifts it without losing the drop.
   - **The tag.** In match a pale, blank luggage tag lies across the case top under the grip, at about x 735-795, y 395-410 at 1080, below the Y of YES. In void it is absent and only the dark zip pulls show. On a straight match cut its disappearance reads as a continuity jump unless it is meant.

2. **Are there 42 local dark outliers over eight levels? I measure fewer.** I compared each pixel with the median of a 15 px window around it.
   - **Centre of the front pool band** (y 545-595, x 300-1000): neither the raw nor the graded frame has a pixel more than 5 levels below its local median. The deepest is about -1 raw and -3 graded. The 4c5ff43 raw had 89 pixels beyond 8 levels in the same band.
   - **Whole lit front of the pool** (y 535-600, x 150-1150, pixels above 40): the raw frame has 17 pixels beyond 8 levels and 23 beyond 5. All 17 lie on one short line at x 1110-1122, y 535-542. That line is the lower end of the diagonal board joint described below, not a mark in the open floor. The high-pass standard deviation of the floor is about 0.9 levels.
   - **The old squiggles:** the handwriting-like marks at y 575-590 in the old frame are gone. The bags wear mask in void_stage_set.stage_floor works.

   What remains are two straight hardboard joints. Both come from the floor's brick pattern, which lays 1.22 x 2.44 m sheets in world space:
   - **The row joint** runs at world y = 0, just behind the bags' centre. It crosses the pool behind the duffel's foot at y 503-506, about 3-6 levels below the floor.
   - **The end joint** of a sheet lies 0.96 m right of the bags' centre and runs toward the lens through the front row of sheets. It shows as a diagonal on the right, from about (1065, 505) to (1130, 550). It is up to 23 raw levels (12 graded) below the local floor, inside the lit pool where the raw floor is about 104 (120 at the centre).

   They are straight, so they read as boards rather than letters. But the diagonal is the most visible mark on the lit floor, and at first glance it reads as a scratch.

3. **Does the foreground stay plain through a slow editorial push? Yes, as a surface.** A 4 % push magnifies by 1.04 and reveals no new structure, because apart from the two joints the floor has none at this scale. In a centred push the pool stays inside the frame: at 720 its left edge moves from 110 to 89, its right edge from 1160 to 1181, and its bottom from about 600 to 610. Nothing new enters and no edge is cut.

   Three caveats:
   - **The push has not been demonstrated.** match_to_void.mp4 is two static plates of 48 frames each, with no push in it.
   - **The plate is too small.** It is 1280x720, already upscaled 1.5x in the 1920 composite and 1.56x by the end of the push. The bag edges and the rim will soften visibly.
   - **The grain would scale with the image.** The graded JPEG has the grade's grain and vignette baked in, and the type previews use that JPEG. Pushing that still would scale a frozen grain pattern, which reads as dirt on the lens, not film grain. Push the raw plate, then apply shoot.py's grade and grain to each frame.

4. **The type over this plate: the title, YES and WHEN?.** I assume a slow centred move of about 4 %. COVERAGE plans a pull back on 'WHEN? held' (6.5 s). What matters is the tightest point of either move.
   - **The field is good.** YES spans y 67-286 and x 676-1223 at 1080, in off-white (236/232/225). Behind it the haze reads 20-28 graded, with no beam edge, joint or haze structure to fight the letterforms.
   - **The spacing is not good.** The top of the case handle is at about y 321 at 1080, so the gap is 35 px, about 3 % of the frame height. A centred 4 % push moves the handle up to about 312, leaving about 26 px. The type is 220 px tall, 20 % of the frame height, so by the end of the push it sits on the handle like a lid.
   - **WHEN? is worse.** It is wider than YES and centred on the same point, so its W spans directly over the handle (about x 687-772 at 1080) with the same air.
   - **The cold open already collides.** The second YES is a straight cut to the registered match plate at z 1.09, centred on (0.5, 0.56) (PLATE.yes in gfx/type.html). I simulated that composite: the handle top lands at about y 231, and its right post runs into the left foot of the Y (x 741-821, baseline about 283).

   You need roughly 90-100 px of air at 1080. Either lower the bags in both registered plates (the shift fix) or make the type smaller and higher. That is the lead's call in gfx/type.html, but the plates should give it room.

5. **The rest of the stage (not revised in this batch).** dawn, dawn_high, cell_close and cell_far are byte-identical to the 4c5ff43 renders.
   - **dawn** still shows the flat cap, the bell cuffs, the tube trousers and the corrugated shirt, and the figure reads as a man.
   - **cell_close** still shows the hard arc behind the shaft and the shaft dying above the patch. The barred patch reads as flat white cards laid on the floor: six evenly bright panes (about 190 graded) with crisp edges on lit floor (about 140). The first pane's end runs into the bunk's black shadow (about 26).
   - **cell_far** predates the seated Dawn that the code now puts in it.
   - **The six new cameras** the cut uses (pool, chair, cell_dawn, dawn_close, cell_floor, divide) have never been published.

   These keep cast at 4 and materials and set_dressing at 5 for the stage. The code fixes since 4c5ff43 need new frames before they can count.

fixes.camera: dawn, dawn_high, cell_close, cell_far, plus pool, chair, cell_dawn, dawn_close, cell_floor, divide
fixes.fix:
Re-render from the current void_stage.py through scenes/shoot.py at 1280x720 and 64 spp. Render pool and cell_dawn at their final_res of 2560x1440.
- Cover the four published cameras and the six unpublished ones (pool, chair, cell_dawn, dawn_close, cell_floor, divide).
- Publish raw and graded under frames/raw/void_stage/ and frames/graded/void_stage/ in one commit with bags, so the stage is judged as one batch.

Before publishing, check these targets in dbg_dawn and dbg_dawn_high (VOID_DEBUG=1):
- hand median about 50-60 graded, with no hand pixel above 1.6x that median;
- the cuff no brighter than the upper arm;
- the bun at least 6 px off the skull outline.

In cell_close, check that the shaft reaches the barred patch over lit floor. In cell_far, check that the seated Dawn reads between the rails.

fixes.problem: This is the film's final title and WHEN? plate, but it is rendered at 1280x720. The 1920 composite is a 1.5x upscale, and a 4 % push makes it 1.56x. That softens the rim line on the case handle and the duffel straps that carry the silhouette. COVERAGE ('WHEN? held') already asks for this plate to be rendered larger for the move. The graded JPEG also has the grade's grain and vignette baked in, and both would scale during a push.
fixes.fix:
Add final_res=(2560, 1440) to CAMERAS['bags'], as 'pool' and 'cell_dawn' already have. shoot.py uses it for final_<cam>.png, and publish_frames.sh accepts any 16:9 frame at least 1280 wide.
- Render it at 64 spp or more, because the rim and haze are low-level and noisy.
- Publish the raw PNG at that size as the push source. The editor then scales the raw plate per frame and applies shoot.py's grade and fresh grain after scaling, never to the graded still.
- Render inspection_room match at the same final_res. Registration does not depend on resolution, but both sides of the cut should be equally sharp under the same move, and the cold open cuts match 9 % tighter.

fixes.problem: There is no air between the type and the bags. YES ends at y 286 and the case handle starts at about y 321 (at 1080). That 35 px gap shrinks to about 26 px at the end of a centred 4 % push, and the type sits on the handle like a lid. The same geometry is in the registered match plate. In the cold open's 9 % cut-in (PLATE.yes: z 1.09, centre (0.5, 0.56)), the handle's right post already runs into the left foot of the Y.
fixes.fix:
Lower the subject in frame with lens shift, not tilt, so the verticals stay straight: set CAMERAS['bags']['shift'] = (0.0, 0.03). apply_camera already reads 'shift'.
- This moves the bags down about 38 px at 720 (about 58 at 1080).
- The pool's front edge goes from about y 600 to about 638 at 720, and to about 650 after a 4 % push, still inside the frame.

inspection_room.py does not read a 'shift' key today. Add the same shift_y to its match camera (set cam.data.shift_y in its camera setup, as void_stage.apply_camera does). Then re-measure the shared vertices so the 0.003 px registration holds.

Even with the shift, the cold open's cut-in at cy 0.56 leaves the handle only about 8 px under the YES. Tell the lead that PLATE.yes needs a centre nearer cy 0.50, or smaller type.

If the match camera cannot take the shift, leave both plates alone. Instead, ask the lead to shrink the type cap height by about 20 % in gfx/type.html and to lower PLATE.yes's centre.

fixes.problem: The blank luggage tag that lies across the case top in inspection_room match is missing from void bags. On a straight match cut, a small pale object vanishes just below the Y of YES and of WHEN?.
fixes.fix:
Carry the tag into the void.
1. In bags(), after loading the case, import inspection_room_set as irs.
2. Call irs.luggage_tag(case, frame, hole=(-0.008, -0.005), grip=(-0.045, 0.542), grip_r=(0.0125, 0.0115)). These are the values inspection_room.py line 932 uses.
3. Build `frame` for the void case the same way inspection_room._case_frame does: Matrix.Translation((gx + x, gy + y, 0.0)) @ Matrix.Rotation(math.radians(-58.0), 4, 'Z').
4. Overlay the edges of the two graded frames and check that the tag's outline registers.

If the tag is deliberately gone at the end, say so in the request, because the cut currently reads as an error.

fixes.problem: (Optional; a judgement call.) Across the cut, Dawn's case drops from a front-pocket median of 75 graded (match) to 28 (void), while the duffel barely changes (14 -> 15). The front still reads: the pocket outline, the zips and the folds are legible. But its left side panel (13-20) is as dark as the black beside it (16-18), and the lower right of its front (22-28) matches the haze to its right (27-31), so only the rim holds those edges. The rim_bags comment says the faces are meant to stay dark, so this is a choice about the last image, not a defect.
fixes.fix:
If the case should keep more of its lead over the duffel, add a soft frontal kicker linked to the case only, in build_bags_island:

kick = st.area('kick_case', (cx - 0.9, cy - 2.6, 0.7), (G[0] + CASE[0], G[1] + CASE[1], 0.33), (0.5, 0.5), 12.0, (0.88, 0.92, 1.0))
st.link_lights([kick], receivers=_meshes(pair[0]), tag='case_kick')

The lamp sits about 1 m left of the lens axis, outside the frame. Adjust its watts to these targets:
- front pocket median about 40-45 graded (p90 about 65);
- left side panel at least 8 levels above the black beside it.

That is still well under match's 75, so the cut keeps its drop. Leave the duffel unlinked, keep rim_bags as it is, and check that the zip pulls do not rise above about 110 graded.

fixes.problem:
The floor's brick pattern (1.22 x 2.44 m sheets in world space) puts two straight joints in the lit pool:
- **The row joint** at world y = 0 crosses behind the duffel's foot (y 503-506, about 3-6 levels below the floor).
- **A sheet's end joint** 0.96 m right of the bags' centre runs toward the lens through the front row. It shows as a diagonal from about (1065, 505) to (1130, 550), up to 23 raw levels (12 graded) below the local floor. It reads as a scratch on the right of the final image's pool, and it accounts for every dark outlier over 8 levels in the lit front band.
fixes.fix:
Move the joints rather than mute them. In void_stage_set.stage_floor, give the brick node an offset vector: br = _brick(nt, _vmath(nt, 'ADD', o, (-0.25, 0.0, 0.0)), 2.44, 1.22, ...). The other nodes keep using `o`.
- This centres the front row's 2.44 m sheet on the bags' centre (world x -40.01).
- Its end joints move to x -41.23 and -38.79, 1.22 m out, which is past the pool's edge (in frame, about x 102 and 1179 at the back of the row, further out toward the lens).
- The back row's end joint moves to x -40.01, which this camera sees only behind the duffel (about x 636-649, y 449-505).
- The row joint behind the bags stays. It reads as a board and keeps the pool from looking like a plain CG disc, which an earlier round flagged.

The offset moves the joints on every island, so re-check dawn, dawn_high and divide.

Muting all joints inside the wear radius would also remove the scratch, but it would leave the pool seamless.

Target: no end joint inside the lit pool, and the row joint no more than about 6 levels below the floor.

fixes.problem: In the published frame (the 4c5ff43 render), the barred patch reads as flat white cards laid on the floor: six evenly bright panes (about 190 graded) with crisp edges on lit floor (about 140). The first pane's end runs into the bunk's black shadow (about 26). The back edge of the top spot's pool is still a hard arc under the shaft.
fixes.fix:
After the priority-1 re-render, if the panes still cut hard:
- **Soften the bar shadows.** Double the window lamp's radius in void_stage_set.cell, from radius=0.05 to about 0.10 in spot('cell_window_light', ...). With the lamp 12 m behind the slot and about 2.6 m from slot to patch, that widens the bar penumbra from about 2 cm to about 4 cm.
- **Lift the black under the bunk** where the first pane ends. Add a weak area fill under the bunk (about 8 W) linked to the cell slab only (ex['slab']), aiming for about 35-40 graded there. lower_bunk_lip cannot do this, because it is linked to the bedding only.
- **Check the arc.** Confirm that SPOTS['cell'] blend 0.50 (0.25 in the published render) has turned it into a roll-off of about 40 cm.
